a: Re-registering a program that is already compiled from the same source recompiles it and makes every retained surface stale
A released program source keeps drawing: `refresh` skips it, while `restore` drops it
`const int A = 2, B = 3;` records neither constant, so arrays sized by either get no locations
Ramp lookups are off by up to half a texel: `t` is used as the texture coordinate with no texel-center remap
b: A released program registration keeps drawing on every renderer that compiled it, and its GPU program is never freed until dispose
After a context restore, a program whose re-registered source failed to compile stops drawing, though before the loss it kept drawing the previous one
A top-level `const int A = 2, B = 3;` records neither constant, so arrays sized by them are dropped from the uniform scan
The id-output rewrite counts `main` and outputs with regexes over the source with comments still in, so a comment mentioning them makes a custom shader unpickable
